subject: Medialyne: evidence & plan request — segmented log retention and deletion cert
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@medialyne.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Medialyne Security <security@medialyne.com>, Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medialyne.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: segmented log retention plan + deletion certification for pilot

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our SIG/CAIQ review for the upcoming pilot, our security team has two specific asks related to customer data retention and deletion:

1) We run a hybrid forensics requirement per customer. For the pilot customers we need an explicit plan that shows how Redwood segments standard operational logs (access/ingest/trace) versus forensic logs, and the retention windows for each segment.

2) We also need a deletion certification template that Redwood can sign once data is destroyed on your end (for purge events and end-of-contract).

Can you provide:
- A short summary (one page) showing log classes + retention windows and controls for segmentation
- A draft deletion certification (PDF) we can review
- Any suggested compensating controls if we ask for 180-day forensic retention for one pilot customer (due to their regulator)

If possible, please get this to us by end of week — our audit lead will kick off the SIG import once we have artifacts.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Cole
Information Security Manager, Medialyne Health
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@medialyne.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: segmented log retention plan + deletion certification for pilot

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Priyom (Product Security) and Rishi (Legal) so we can cover controls + contract language.

Quick summary of our plan — will attach formal artifacts in my follow-up:
- Log segmentation: we classify logs into (a) Operational (metrics, autoscaling events), (b) Audit (auth events, admin actions), (c) Forensics (full request/response captures, debug traces). Each class is stored in separate buckets with role-based access controls and distinct retention policies.
- Default retention: Operational = 30 days, Audit = 365 days, Forensics = 90 days (encrypted at rest).
- For pilot-specific customer exceptions: we can support a longer forensic window (up to 180 days) as a documented exception tied to a signed Data Processing Addendum (DPA) + documented compensating controls: encrypted key split, restricted access logs, and an additional quarterly attestation.
- Deletion certification: we have a template we use for enterprise customers; we will adapt it to include the exception clause and KMS key notice.

Next steps: Priyom will prepare the one-page segmentation matrix and the archival matrix spreadsheet; Rishi will draft the deletion-cert wording and the DPA amendment language. I'll bundle a short guidance note on compensating controls.

We should be able to get drafts to you by EOD Thursday (2027-09-16). Is that timeline acceptable?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
From: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medialyne.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@medialyne.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: segmented log retention plan + deletion certification for pilot

Kimberly — Thursday works. Two clarifying items from our side before you prepare artifacts:

- The pilot customer requires FIPS-validated encryption for forensic data when retained beyond 90 days. Can you confirm whether Redwood can (a) mark the bucket as FIPS, or (b) provide an equivalent proof?
- On deletion certification: we need the certificate to include a hash or manifest of deleted artifacts (file paths and timestamps) where feasible. The manifest can be redacted for PII.

We appreciate the quick turnaround — our auditor is particularly focused on the manifest requirement.

-Paul
Paul Nguyen
Technical Compliance Lead, Medialyne Health
From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>
To: Paul Nguyen <paul.nguyen@medialyne.com>, Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@medialyne.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.inference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 16:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: segmented log retention plan + deletion certification for pilot

Hi Paul/Sarah — attaching the requested artifacts for initial review. See attachments:

- redwood-log-archival-matrix.xlsx: a per-log-class mapping (Operational / Audit / Forensics), default retention, recommended exception governance, and sample IAM roles required to access forensic buckets.
- deletion-certification-template.pdf: editable template including a manifest section (file paths + timestamps) and a redaction field for PII.
- SIG-answers-2027.xlsx: updated answers referencing our retention controls and the exception approval process.

A few important implementation notes:
- FIPS: We rely on customer-managed keys in supported clouds. For pilot customers that require FIPS, we can enable the FIPS-validated KMS option for the forensic bucket and require key usage that fits your compliance needs. We'll include the exact configuration steps in the Drive link.
- Manifest: Our deletion flow produces a manifest with object keys and deletion timestamps. We can provide an attested manifest (hash-signed by our key) in the deletion certificate. Where manifests contain PII, we'll redact fields and provide a separate attestation statement.
- Exception governance: exceptions are allowed via an approved exception request (signed by customer + Redwood) and are reviewed quarterly. Exception requests include the date range, scope, compensating controls, and an expiration date.

Link to artifacts: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2b3C-example-evidence
HubSpot record: HS-28934

If that looks good, Kimberly/Rishi — can we get legal approval language to append to the pilot DPA? We will draft a short statement for the certificate that says: "Redwood Inference certifies that the objects specified in the manifest were deleted from Redwood-managed storage as of the date indicated; attestation provided per the deletion-certification-template."

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Product Security, Redwood Inference
